newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks pare gains to end modestly higher.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks pare gains to end modestly higher.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended Tuesday's session with only modest gains, as the morning's rally ran out of steam and investors reacted to Morgan Stanley's weighting cut for the Hong Kong market, analyst said.
The Hang Seng index closed 11.02 points higher at 11,223.62 after rising to 11,334.40 earlier in the session.
Turnover was HK$4.71 billion, up from Monday's HK$3.2 billion.
"I guess we have just run into levels where the market could not muster any more strength," said Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading at HG Asia.

Brokers said share prices had begun to fade during the afternoon as players discussed last Thursday's reweighting by Morgan Stanley of the Hong Kong and Thai markets. "People were talking about it," said Lesko.

Morgan Stanley said due to concerns about a rise in U.S. interest rates, regional strategist Peter Churchouse had increased the cash weighting in his model portfolio to 15 percent from 10. Hong Kong's weighting dropped to 20.5 percent from 23.0 and Thailand's was cut to 6.5 percent from 9.0.
Futures selling weighed on the market with September Hang Seng futures ending down 45 points at 11,170.
"The concentration is very much on quality," said Robin Hammond, Hong Kong research director at Asia Equity. "Selective (property) developers are still leading the way."
Henderson Land, which is due to report fiscal 1996 results on Wednesday, rose HK$0.25 to HK$61.75.

Hammond said the market had overreacted at the start of trade to overnight gains on Wall Street. The Hang Seng notched up a 121.80 point gain in early trade after rising 187.01 points on Monday. The Dow industrials rose 73.98 points to 5,733.84.
Analysts said the invitation to Hong Kong to join the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) had not affected trading.
"I don't think as an isolated event it would have much impact. It just means higher profile as a financial hub," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
Hong Kong and China Gas fell HK$0.05 to HK$12.80. It posted interim net profit of HK$979.1 million versus HK$815.4 million.
Wharf shares were unmoved by news that companies involved in Hong Kong's long delayed Container Terminal Number Nine project have agreed on a proposal which will be submitted to China for approval.
Wharf ended unchanged at HK$29.95. Hutchison rose HK$0.10 to HK$48.20. -- Jennifer Genevieve (852) 2843 6345
